source.title: SGD and Weight Decay Secretly Minimize the Rank of Your Neural Network
source.authors: Tomer Galanti; Zachary S. Siegel; A. Gupte; T. Poggio

record.tranche_reason: It varies batch size and measures both training fit and test performance, conceptually testing whether batch size changes the generalization gap; its main intervention and measured property are not the original claim’s memorization or sharpness measures.
record.gate_note: The paper also measures average weight-matrix rank across learning-rate, weight-decay, and batch-size settings. Those rank results do not measure the behavior named by V1–V8; they are summarized under fits_no_version. Rank values and most accuracy curves appear in figures without extractable numeric values.
record.test_reason: The study directly varies SGD batch size and measures held-out classification accuracy under a fixed epoch budget, testing V5 with the same basic intervention and measure as its original studies.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is accurate but omits the main conclusion: SGD with weight decay biases learned weight matrices toward lower rank, especially with smaller batches, higher learning rates, or stronger weight decay. The authors describe its generalization effect as marginal and report a slight performance association, without establishing that lower rank causes better generalization.
record.recipe_differences: The study varies batch size and evaluates train and test accuracy on naturally labeled CIFAR10, rather than testing random-label memorization or comparing batch-size generalization gaps as a primary outcome.
record.method_sensitivity: Test performance tends to improve with smaller batch sizes in the reported ResNet-18 CIFAR10 sweep; the paper says the effect of low-rank bias on test performance is marginal.

fits_no_version.finding: Theoretical bounds and experiments associate smaller batches, higher learning rates, and stronger weight decay with lower effective weight-matrix rank; the batch-size influence on rank is minimal without weight decay.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: SGD with weight decay induces a hyperparameter-dependent bias toward low-rank weight matrices.

fits_no_version.finding: The authors associate lower average rank with slightly better test performance among models that perfectly fit training data.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Effective weight-matrix rank can correlate with held-out performance within a fixed architecture and training-fit condition.

record.problems: The test-performance relationship is reported qualitatively and appears in figures without extractable numeric values or uncertainty estimates. The generalization experiment is limited to ResNet-18 on CIFAR10 and the authors describe the effect as marginal.
record.rows_left_out: No additional version-matching rows. Rank measurements across batch size, learning rate, and weight decay do not measure a named version’s specified behavior; their qualitative findings are summarized under fits_no_version. Numeric figure values are not recoverable from the supplied text.

untested.parts: Random-label fitting and held-out performance compared with natural labels.
Width sweeps beyond the width required for zero training error.
Controlled comparisons of convolutional and fully connected architectures, including learned local connectivity or transferred initialization.
Adaptive optimizers versus SGD, tuning budgets, optimizer switching, and decoupled weight decay.

Language models, identification of workload-dependent batch thresholds, longer-training remedies, and controlled tests of learning-rate scaling, warmup, or normalization and regularization adaptations.
Controlled dropout interventions; the architectural use or replacement of dropout does not test its effect.
Magnitude-aware sharpness, its association with generalization gaps, and comparisons with norm- or margin-based measures.
Removing memorized training examples and comparing the accuracy loss with random removal.

missing.what: Additional batch-size sweeps report train and test accuracy for MLP-BN-10-100, RES-BN-5-500, ViT, ResNet-18, and VGG-16. These accuracy results bear on V5 and are incorrectly excluded by rows_left_out as though they were only rank measurements. Extract condition-specific comparisons; curve directions and effect sizes cannot be read from the supplied text.
missing.locator: Appendix B.1–B.2, Figures 7–9 and 11–12. Non-ViT models train for 500 epochs; ViT trains for 200 epochs.

record.verdict_notes: The marginal-effect statement concerns low-rank bias and does not establish that the batch-size accuracy difference is negligible or statistically non-significant. The supplied figure text contains axes and legends but no readable curves, so additional model-specific verdicts cannot be assigned reliably.

versions.untested_parts: No random-label training or comparison of random-label and natural-label test accuracy.
No width sweep across the interpolation threshold with test error measured.
No comparison of convolutional and fully connected networks.
No comparison of adaptive optimizers with SGD.

The paper varies batch size for ResNet-18 on CIFAR10 at fixed learning rate and weight decay and reports the test-performance trend, but does not test language models, workload-dependent thresholds, or recipe adaptations such as longer training or learning-rate warmup.
The paper measures rank, not magnitude-aware sharpness or the ranking of generalization gaps against norm- or margin-based measures.

rows.subject: ResNet-18
rows.operation_detail: Varied batch size while keeping learning rate and weight decay constant; selected settings so models perfectly fit the training data.
rows.value: Models trained with smaller batch sizes tend to have a better test performance.
rows.note: The authors state the qualitative trend; the figure does not provide extractable numeric test-accuracy values in the supplied text.
rows.check: The qualitative result is supported by Section 4.2. Specify the within-panel smaller-batch comparator and the three Figure 4 settings: initial learning rate/weight decay = 0.001/0.006, 0.005/0.006, and 0.01/0.0004. Learning rates are matched across batch sizes within each panel but decrease tenfold at epochs 60, 100, and 200. Training includes augmentation and zero momentum. Exact accuracy differences and uncertainty cannot be recovered from the supplied text.

relationships.condition: ResNet-18 on CIFAR10; batch sizes 4–128; matched learning-rate schedules and weight decay within each Figure 4 panel; 500 epochs.
relationships.reason: R1 records the authors' explicit smaller-batch test-performance advantage when all models fit the training data perfectly; its magnitude is not recoverable.
relationships.display_finding: The study reports better test performance with smaller batches despite perfect training fits, but this comparison remains unverified and its magnitude is unavailable.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.

reader_labels.label: supports
reader_labels.condition: ResNet-18 on CIFAR10, batch-size sweep at fixed learning rate and weight decay for 500 epochs
reader_labels.reason: With training fit held perfect, the authors report better test performance for smaller batches (R1). This is a qualitative trend, and the authors characterize the performance effect as marginal.
